title: Compliance Delivery Orchestration with Smart Formatting and Digest Checks
creator: Aisha Nader
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers need periodic, auditable delivery of compliance artifacts (PDF/CSV bundles, index manifests) that respect tenant residency rules and retention policies. Current ad-hoc export runners produce large monolithic archives with inconsistent format choices, minimal integrity metadata, and fragile delivery (timeouts, SFTP failures). This causes support overhead and slow audit responses.

Goal: Design and ship a delivery orchestration layer that: (1) negotiates best-fit formats per-tenant (PDF vs CSV vs compressed NDJSON), (2) produces signed integrity manifests (SHA256 + signing key fingerprint) for every export bundle, (3) respects data residency routing for temporary staging and final storage, (4) supports scheduled and ad-hoc exports with retry/backoff and delivery channels (presigned URL, SFTP, secure webhook), and (5) exposes delivery and audit status in Console + downloadable evidence dashboard.

Scope: This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, and orchestration policies. Implementation will be split into backend worker, store adapters, signing service integration, and Console UI pieces (scheduler UX, delivery history, manifest viewer). It explicitly does NOT include on-prem agent packaging for air-gapped customers (follow-up epic).

Constraints & non-goals: Keep runtime resource usage bounded (avoid full in-memory dumps for tenants >100GB). Prefer stream-first generation and chunked packaging. Ensure exported artifacts are encrypted-in-transit and at rest per tenant KMS choices. Work with Security early for signing key lifecycle and audit logging.

Stakeholders: Compliance PM (Aisha), Eng owners: Diego (core exports), Mei Chen (storage/kms), Ravi Patel (console), Security reviewer: Lena Ortega.

Success metrics (initial):
- Scheduled exports succeed end-to-end for 95% of tenants on first attempt in a 30-day pilot window.
- Time-to-first-deliverable for a 50GB tenant <= 6 hours using streaming + chunking.
- Console shows manifest verification status with download counts and per-tenant residency stamp.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler: Admins can create a tenant-scoped recurring export job that selects: date range, format preference (pdf/csv/ndjson), delivery channel (presigned-url/sftp/webhook), and retention policy to apply to produced artifacts.
Format negotiation: For each tenant job the orchestration picks the most compact supported format if 'auto' is chosen; UI shows the chosen format and rationale.

Manifest: Every exported bundle includes a machine-readable manifest (NDJSON) with per-file SHA256, total bundle checksum, created_by job id, tenant residency tag, and signing fingerprint. Manifest is accompanied by a detached signature produced via our Signing Service.
Residency: Exports are staged only in clouds/regions approved for tenant residency; staging S3 buckets must have region tag and retention TTL matching tenant policy.
Delivery reliability: The system retries delivery with exponential backoff; failures for >3 attempts create an incident ticket stub in Console and notify tenant admins by email/webhook.

Observability: Console shows pipeline traces, file-level progress, size estimates, and artifact verification status. Metrics emitted: export.success, export.failure, manifest.verify_pass, manifest.verify_fail.
Security: Signing keys rotate per policy and signing operations are logged to the audit trail; security review completed and approved before GA.
Backwards compatibility: Existing one-off export API remains functional; new scheduler endpoints and new manifest schema are additive and versioned.
Developer docs: Runbook and architecture diagram published to Confluence with example webhook payloads and sample manifest verification script.
Customer test: Run pilot with two tenants in different regions (EU, US) validating residency routing, delivery to SFTP, and manifest digest verification by customer security team.
